full_judgment:
Quazi Reza-Ul Hoque, J: In the instant writ petition Rule NISI was issued calling upon the respondent No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 25.10.2007 passed by the learned District Judge, Sirajganj in Artha Rin Miscellaneous Appeal No. 01 of 2006 condoning the delay of 7 years 10 months and 7 days and admitting the appeal for hearing (annexure-A) should not be declared to have been done without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/ or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. And pending hearing of the Rule, the operation of the impugned order was stayed for a period of three (3) months, which was extended from time to time, lastly on 08.07.2010 till disposal of the Rule. 

 2. The petitioners case, in short, is that the respondent No.1 as plaintiff filed Money Suit No. 13/1986 against Angaha Pat Chaski (APACHAS), Raiganj Unit No. 3, Raiganj and 5(five) others including the petitioner as defendant No. 2 for recovery of money in the Court of learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, Sirajganj, stating inter alia that under Bangladesh Jute Project, IDA Credit-765-RD to provide marketing Credit to marketing Centres, during 1982-83 season, Angsha Pat ChashiSamity (ARACHAS), Raiganj Unit No. 3, the defendant No. 1, the present petitioner was as its President was sanctioned with a loan cash credit limit of TK. 4,00,000/-(four lacs) by the plaintiff bank by letter No. RCD05/-29/40 dated 10.08.1982 at a simple interest rate of 12% per annum. The loan was repayable and fully adjustable by 30.04.1983. The then Jute Extension Officer Abdul Kuddus has been succeeded by defendant No. 5 and defendant Nos. 2- 5 were jointly and severally liable for the debt and repayment of the loan as it was secured through a Demand Promissory Note amounting to Tk. 4 lacs on 29.11.82 in favour of the plaintiff bank. The defendants failed to repay the loan. The service charges and penal interests were stipulated at the rate of 4% and 6% respectively per annum. 

 4. On 21.05.1988 the suit was decreed ex parte behind the back of the petitioner, without considering the actual facts and circumstances and true evidences on record. After coming to know about the ex pane decree against him the defendant-petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 30/90 by filing an application under order- 9, rule- 13 of the Civil Procedure Code, 1908 to cancel and set aside the ex parte decree and re-instate the suit to its original file and number. The learned Judge of the Artho Rin Adalat, after hearing the said petition on 23.01.1991 rejected the said petition. 

 5. The defendant- petitioner after coming to know from a news item in the Daily Janakantha dated 06.05.1997 that the scheduled property of the original Money Suit No. 77 of 1996, corresponding Execution Case No. 9 of 1994 will be auction-sold, filed Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1997 under order 21, rule 58 read with section 151 of the Civil Procedure Code stating inter alia that he is not at all indebted to the opposite party bank. The father of the petitioner sold a portion of the scheduled property else where long ago. The petitioner's brother, sister and wife are the owners of the rest of the scheduled property and therefore the same is not liable to be auctioned. The judgment-creditor has illegally obtained a decree for auction, and as such, the petitioner is entitled to be exonerated from the obligation of the suit. 

 7. The opposite party No. 1, i.e. bank, filed written objection stating inter alia that the petitioner as Chairman of the Angsha Pat Chashi Samity, Raiganj Unit- 3 took a loan of TK. 75,000/- from the bank and did not repay the same according to the terms of the loan for which the opposite party bank filed Money Suit No. 13 of 1986 for recovery of the loan and got a decree on 22.05.1988. Due to non-payment of the decreetal amount the Execution Case No. 14 of 1989 was filed against the petitioner and others and after establishment of Artha Rin Adalat the case was transferred and re-numbered as Artha Rin Case No. 77 of 1990 and then after transfer to the Artho Rin Adalat No. 2, it was re-numbered as Case No. 9 of 1994. The scheduled property of the petitioner was attached on 14.11.1990 and the same was approved by the Court on 26.11.1990. The case of the petitioner is barred by limitation and suffers from defect of parties; and the scheduled land is owned and possessed by the petitioner. 

 8. Artha Rin Adalat- 2 framed only one issue as to whether the petitioner is entitled to get the remedy as prayed for and on careful perusal of the papers and evidence on record the Court found that the loan of TK. 75,000/-drawn by the petitioner as Chairman of the Samity has already been adjusted by purchasing 500 mounds of jute at the rate of TK. 150/- per mound and keeping the same in bknk's godown, which had been admitted by the bank and subsequently by selling the said jute by the bank and depositing the sale proceeds in the account of the Samity, the loan was fully adjusted and the same had been admitted by the bank in a letter addressed to the Samity. After considering papers and evidence on record and the depositions made on behalf of the parties the learned Artha Rin Adalat came to the finding that the petitioner is entitled to get the relief as prayed for and allowed the Miscellaneous Case on contest passed on order on 23.08.1998 to release suit property from the schedule of the Execution Case No. 9 of 1994. 

 9. The opposite party bank filed Artho Rin Miscellaneous Appeal No. 1 of 2006 on 20.08.2006 in the Court of District Judge, Sirajganj against the said judgment and order along with an application for condonation of delay of 7 years 10 months and 7 days under section 5 of the Limitation Act read with section 57 of the Artha Rin Ain. The Court of Appeal below on 25.10.2007, that is, after filing of the appeal and the condonation petition in the court of the learned District Judge and registering the same as Miscellaneous Appeal No. 01 of 2006 on 20.08.2006 the condonation petition was disposed of 25.10.2007, condoning the delay and allowing the appeal (annexure- A and A 1 ). 

 10. Mr. Abul Kalam, the learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner submitted that the Artho Rin Adalat disposed of the Miscellaneous Case No. 01 of 1997 on 23.08.1998 and according to Artho Rin Adalat Ain an appeal against the judgment and order should have been filed within 30 days. But the opposite party bank sent the relevant papers to the learned lawyer on 13.10.1998 i.e. on the 30th day of passing of the judgment and order consuming the whole period of limitation sitting idle. So there is serious laches and negligence on the part of the appellant bank. Therefore it was not possible on the part of the learned lawyer to file the appeal within the statutory limitation of 30 days after receiving the relevant papers on the 30th day after passing of the judgment and order. 

 15. The impugned Order passed by the learned District Judge, Sirajganj dated 25.10.07 in Artha Rin Miscellaneous Appeal No. 01 of 2006, is hereby declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and therefore it is set aside.
